scope: Forward military cargo actually discharged or redistributed into the Marshall main network, with Kusaie/Ponape tracked separately. This is not national shipping output.
guards: No historical 4-Dec mass Kwajalein/Roi carrier raid is auto-imported after the revised GALVANIC carrier damage/mission state.
Branch cargo-utilization/turnaround gains improve useful delivered tonnage; they do not create merchant hulls.
US submarines and late-Dec Gilbert-based air pressure remain real; no immunity is credited.
Troop reinforcement remains bounded near historical planned Central-Pacific reinforcement scale; the main Branch delta is equipment/material completion, not a second army appearing on the atolls.
loss_mechanisms: 1-2 medium transport/auxiliary losses or mission kills plus weather/submarine/air-threat aborts and inter-atoll unloading friction; exact hull names remain open.

eastern_carolines_separate_delivery.main_use: garrison reinforcement, runway/staging completion, seaplane/harbor support, power/communications, engineer plant and reserve stores; not added to Marshall local combat OOB

personnel_flow.rule: Most are historically plausible planned reinforcements or reallocation. Do not add these on top of a later garrison total that already includes Jan arrivals.
personnel_flow.Marshall_midJan_total_guard: Use roughly 26,500-28,500 personnel in the Marshall proper as the total-scale work band; Kwajalein/Roi-Namur roughly 8,200-8,900. Do not exceed this without named-unit trace.
personnel_flow.Kusaie_note: Kusaie remains a separate eastern-Carolines garrison, roughly 4,000-class plus dated Jan reinforcement; not part of Marshall total.

time_phases.effect: Emergency redistribution and first reinforcement cycle while US Gilbert bases are only beginning to turn into sustained air-pressure nodes. Highest marginal value for construction plant, wire/cable, ammunition dispersion, radar/power spares and aviation support.
Organized convoy cycle through Truk/Ponape/Kusaie. US long-range/photo pressure rises; daylight inter-atoll movement becomes less attractive. Night unloading and dispersal increase turnaround cost.

Forward delivery remains possible but progressively dangerous. More cargo is discharged west/central nodes and redistributed by small craft at night; completion rather than new giant projects becomes priority.

strategic_allocation_logic: Japan does not know Kwajalein will be the direct main target. Taroa/Wotje/Mili still attract substantial investment as plausible stepping-stones; Kwajalein/Roi gets C2/lagoon/base-system reinforcement; Eniwetok gets western staging/recovery value. Some material is therefore deliberately 'wasted' on strongpoints the US may bypass.
